Priya: Heads-up — bringing up paloma12b (v1-int4) on canary pool-7. Seeing sporadic OOMs on long summarization runs and a small BLEU/ROUGE dip (~1.8 pts). Root log: `kv_cache_allocate failed`
Rhein: What runtime flags? prefetch / batch window / max_new_tokens?
Priya: Runtime: prefetch=true, continuous_batching=true, microbatch=6, slot_reserve=0.06, max_new_tokens=300. Repro pattern: long-document -> ~900 generated tokens; failures around 650-800 tokens.
Maya: Quick idea: fragmentation rather than peak usage. Do we have slot_frag metrics? Also try disabling prefetch and lowering max_new_tokens to 150 for a sanity run.
Priya: Grabbed node snippet: ```
ERROR OOM kv_alloc; total_used=12.4GB total_free=0.4GB slot_frag=0.28
alloc_stack: ...
```
ops-bot: Canary deploy started: paloma12b-int4 -> pool-7 (job 4865432101)
Rhein: slot_frag 0.28 = bad. Short-term candidates: 1) prefetch=false + max_new_tokens=150; 2) enable compact_on_evict=true; 3) reduce concurrent requests (max_parallel_requests=2). Which to try first?
Priya: Spinning up #1 now: `curl -X POST https://canary/api/serve -d '{"model":"paloma12b-int4","cfg":{"prefetch":false,"max_new_tokens":150}}'` (job 4865432102)
Maya: Also start an A/B eval: int4 vs int8 on 400 summarization prompts. If int8 has no quality drop, might need per-channel quant calibration for attention/kv.
Priya: Update: after disabling prefetch + 150 max_new_tokens we ran ~1.7k requests, zero OOMs. p50 latency +10ms, cost +7%. Kicking off int8 A/B (job 4865432109).
Rhein: Nice. If stable, rollout proposal: keep int4 default but set conservative defaults: max_new_tokens=150, prefetch=false, monitor slot_frag and OOM_rate for 24-48h. Plan to enable compact_on_evict and raise slot_compactor_threshold to 0.15 as a subsequent change.
Maya: Add automatic safety gates: rollback if OOM_rate > 0.05% or ROUGE drops > 1.2 pts on the eval set. Also log `nvidia-smi` + allocator traces on any future OOMs.
Priya: Will add alerts and the roll-forward checklist. Will post the int8 vs int4 eval numbers when complete. Thanks :thumbsup:
